faqs.question: What does the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Nail measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the presence of fungal organisms in a nail sample.

faqs.question: Why is the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Nail done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose fungal nail infections and determine appropriate treatment options • To identify the specific type of fungus causing the infection • To assess the severity and extent of fungal nail infection • To monitor the effectiveness of antifungal treatment

faqs.question: When is the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Nail recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test may be recommended if you have • thickened, discoloured, or brittle nails suggestive of a fungal infection, • a previous diagnosis of fungal nail infection, • recurrent or persistent nail infections, or • symptoms indicative of fungal nail infection, such as pain or discomfort.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Nail are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results indicate the presence of fungal organisms, confirming a fungal nail infection.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Nail?
faqs.answer: During this test, a nail sample will be collected in a sterile container. The sample will be sent to the laboratory for culture and identification of the fungus.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Nail?
faqs.answer: • Keep the affected nails clean and dry before sample collection. • Do not apply any nail polish or artificial nails to the affected nails. • Inform your doctor about any antifungal medications you may be taking. Also, tell them if you have any specific requirements. • Follow any additional instructions provided by your doctor.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Nail?
faqs.answer: • KOH smear: A microscopic examination of a nail sample to detect fungal elements • Dermatophyte test: A rapid screening test to detect dermatophyte fungal infections • Histopathology: Examination of a nail biopsy under a microscope to determine the presence of fungal infection or other abnormalities

faqs.question: What is the Fungal Culture and Identification test - Nail also known as?
faqs.answer: Nail Fungus Culture or Onychomycosis Culture

faqs.question: What is onychomycosis?
faqs.answer: Onychomycosis is a common fungal infection of the nails. It can affect both fingernails and toenails, causing thickening, discolouration, and brittleness. Onychomycosis is usually caused by dermatophytes, yeasts, or molds and can be challenging to treat without proper diagnosis.
